notes: Page 2 is a preparation page (build on a table, not on the grass/floor; open only bag 1 first). It has no building steps, so no pieces or joins are added.

As on page 4, pieces are given in `parts` and rests_on relations as `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field.

The images are small and the step drawings are ambiguous. Step 5 appears to show only the result of step 4, and I added nothing for it. Step 7 appears to show the result of step 6. Exact stud ports and the placement of b6 (right-end slope, not clearly introduced) and b11 (black corner plate in step 8) are best guesses.
Technic bricks b4/b5 appear dark gray in the drawings but are black per the parts list/page 4.

Page 6 builds the cockpit sub-assembly (boxed steps 1-5) and then attaches it to the chassis in step 9. As on earlier pages, pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field.

Sub-assembly: step 1 white 6x8 plate (b12); step 2 two white 1x4 bricks as side walls (b13, b14); step 3 red 2x2 corner brick (b15) with a red seat (b16) on it, and a red 1x2 brick (b18) with a red seat (b17) on it; step 4 red steering stand (b19) between the seats; step 5 two white 2x3 bricks (b20 at the left side, b21 at the front) built up beside the seat area. Sticker 15 (a '5' badge) is not modelled.

Step 9: the cockpit sub-assembly is attached next to the chassis (b1-b11). I assumed the 6x8 plate b12 clutches the free studs of the two red 1x6 plates b1 and b2. The drawing is ambiguous, as it could also sit on the Technic bricks.
The drawings are small. The piece types for the walls in step 2 and the bricks in step 5 are inferred from the parts list (white 1x4 and 2x3 bricks), and the stud ports are approximate.
Page 7 (steps 10-12). As on earlier pages, pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field.

Step 10 adds red pieces at the rear of the cockpit, behind the seats and beside the gray plate. I modelled them as a red 2x2 corner brick (b22) and a red 2x2 plate (b23). The red inventory is limited, and the drawing does not show clearly which red pieces they are.

Step 11 adds a white 2x2 corner plate (b24, shown with arrows) on the back-left white slope. The red stack looks taller in the step 11 and 12 drawings. This probably comes from more red pieces being added, but I could not identify them reliably and did not add them.
Step 12 adds the white curved wedge brick with 4 studs (b25) over the rear gray plate and white plate. Its exact support (b8 and b3) is a best guess.
Stud ports are approximate. The step drawings are small and ambiguous.
Page 8 starts a new sub-assembly (the nose / front section of the Mach 5). Pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field.

Steps 1-4: a white 2x2 corner plate (b26) with a white 1x2 plate (b27) on it, the white wedged inverted 4x4 brick (b28) on top, then a red 2x2 plate (b29). Step 5: two white 1x8 plates (b30, b31) extend backwards from the wedge. Step 6: two black Technic 1x4 bricks (b32, b33), one on each long plate. Step 7: a white 2x8 plate (b34) across the Technic bricks and a dark bluish gray 2x4 plate (b35) on top of them.

Only one red 2x2 plate (3022) is in the parts list, and it is used here (b29). The red 2x2 plate I assigned on page 7 (b23) was a guess and is probably a different red piece, most likely the red 2x2 corner brick.

Where the long plates b30/b31 attach to the wedge b28 (and whether they also touch b26), and the stud ports, are approximate. This sub-assembly will presumably be joined to the chassis on a later page.
Page 9 (steps 8-10, the 2x sub-assembly, and step 13). Pieces are in `parts`/`repeats` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field.

Step 14: two long gray plates are added beside the black plate on the nose, over the Technic bricks. I read them as dark bluish gray 1x6 plates (b38, b39); the drawing is small and they could be the 1x4 gray plates instead.

Page 13 (steps 20-21). Pieces are in `parts`/`repeats` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field. The drawings are small, so these are best guesses.
Step 20: three stepped white curved 4x1 bricks (b57-b59) are added on the nose/hood. Their supports are approximate. Stickers 16, 17 and 18 (the red 'M' hood design) in step 21 are not modelled.

Page 16 (steps 4-7), the Snake Oiler chassis. Pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field. The step drawings are dark and small, so identifications are best guesses.

Step 8: the cockpit sub-assembly is attached to the chassis. I assumed b72 rests on the black long plates b60/b61 and the black corner plate b70, as for the Mach 5. Stud ports are approximate.
Page 18. Pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field. The step drawings are small, so these are best guesses.

Step 9: a black bracket 5x2x2 1/3 (b83, type 6087, inset drawing) is placed at the left of the cockpit, on the black corner plate b70 and the chassis. The black bracket on the Mach 5 (page 5, b37) was recorded as a 1x2-1x4 bracket (2436), but it is probably also a 5x2 bracket (6087), as the shapes match. The list has four 6087 and only one 2436.

Boxed steps 1-6 start a new sub-assembly, the Snake Oiler rear/engine section: two black Technic 1x6 bricks (b84, b85) joined by a black Technic 1x4 (b87); orange 1x2 plates (b88, b89); a blue 4x4 plate (b90); an orange inverted slope (b91); a yellow 2x3 plate (b92); two lime round 1x1 plates (b93, b94) as lights; two red 1x4 plates (b95, b96) and a light bluish gray 1x4 plate (b97) in step 6. The small black plate drawn under the lower brick in step 1 is not modelled, and the exact identity of the black block in step 2 is a guess. Stickers are not modelled. Stud ports are approximate.

Page 19 adds no new pieces. Step 10 pushes the rear sub-assembly (b84-b97 from page 18) up onto the underside of the black bracket b83, so its yellow plate b92 clutches the bracket. Step 11 just turns the model over. The edges here are the only additions; stud ports are approximate.
Page 20 (steps 12-13). Pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field. The model is shown upside-up again after the flip on page 19.

Step 12 already shows two black 4x2 wedge plates (b98 left, b99 right) forming a pointed deck over the bracket and yellow plate. The drawing does not show them being added, so I recorded them here. The dark bluish gray 1x6 plate (b100, arrows) is then added across the orange wall and the wedge. Step 13: a black 2x2 corner plate (b101, arrows) is placed on the wedge/gray plate.
Supports and stud ports are approximate. Small drawings make the exact stud positions ambiguous.
Page 21 (steps 14-15). Pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field.

Step 14: four orange wheel arches (b102-b105) are added at the four wheel positions; three are drawn already in place, and the right-far one is shown with arrows. Step 15: a black 1x3 plate (b106) at the left wall and an orange cheese slope (b107) on the right-far arch, both with arrows.
Supports and stud ports are approximate; I could not tell exactly which bricks each arch clutches.
Page 22 (steps 16-17). Pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field. The drawings are small and dark, so these are best guesses.

Step 16: a black curved 2x4 (b108) over the rear engine area; two orange side-handle plates (b109 in place, b110 with arrows); a light bluish gray 1x4 plate (b111) across the cockpit rear; and two orange wedge plates (b112, b113) over the rear/side wheel arches.

Step 17: the boxed sub-assembly is two orange wedge plates (b114, b115) with an orange 1x6 grooved tile (b116) on top, forming the rear wing, fitted on the rear arch. Stickers 13 and 5 are not modelled.
The gray cross strip in step 16 is read as a 1x4 plate. Supports and stud ports are approximate.
Page 23 (step 18 only). Pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field.

Step 18 adds two black curved 4x1 bricks (b117, b118) as the rear fins on the orange wedge plates. The black fins' supports and ports are approximate. Small black plates around them (near the rear arch and cockpit rear) may also be new, but they could not be identified from the drawing and are not modelled.
Page 24 (step 19). Pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field.
The inset shows a black curved wedge brick 4x4 with no top studs (b119) with stickers 3, 4 and 7 (the black 'engine intake' piece), placed at the rear behind the seats. Stickers are not modelled.

The model also now shows black curved side panels along the cockpit sides, which I read as the two remaining black curved 4x1 bricks (b120, b121). That is inferred from the parts list (four black 61678 in total, two used on page 23), and their positions are approximate. Stud ports are approximate.

Page 25 (step 20, 2x). An orange curved 3x1 brick is pushed onto each of the two lime round 1x1 plates (b93, b94) at the rear of the chassis, so they act as the rear lights. The lime plates are the ones placed on the rear sub-assembly on page 18. Copy 1 attaches to b93 and copy 2 to b94, which is inferred from the drawing.
Page 26 (step 21). Pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field. The drawing is small, so these are best guesses.

Step 21: the second trans-clear curved windscreen (b122) is placed over the cockpit front. The front body is dressed with more orange pieces carrying stickers 19-24 (not modelled). Stickers 21 and 24 are on the two curved bricks from page 25; I read the other stickers (20, 23 on curved bricks, 19, 22 on cheese slopes) as four new orange pieces (b123-b126). That is inferred and approximate.

Page 27 (step 22 only). Pieces are in `parts` and rests_on relations are `joined` edges because this schema has no `pieces` field.

Step 22 shows a stepped orange nose cover added at the front of the car, in front of the black hood. I could not tell the exact pieces from the drawing. I recorded two orange curved 3x1 bricks (b129, b130), the last two of that type in the parts list. The stepped layers may also include orange tiles or plates. Supports (the red plate b95 and gray plate b97) and ports are approximate.
The white rod hanging below the front is the handle part from page 26 (b128).

Copy 2 goes through the two dark bluish gray Technic bricks b63/b64 at the other end (pin-hole.2 assumed). The assignment is inferred from the arrow positions.
Stickers 25-32 on the orange hood layers are not modelled; no new bricks are added in this step.

The Snake Oiler minifigure driver is shown seated but is not in the parts list and is not modelled. Stickers 28 and 30 are not modelled.

Page 31 is a parts inventory page (illustrated parts list with quantities) with no building steps, so it adds no pieces or joins.

The inventory shows black 5 x 2 brackets with a quantity of 4 and a single black 1 x 2 - 1 x 4 bracket. Both Mach 5 and Snake Oiler brackets in earlier steps are probably the 5 x 2 type (lego-6087). The Mach 5 bracket recorded on page 5 as b37 (lego-2436) is likely a 6087 as well.
Page 32 is an advertisement for other Speed Racer sets (8160 Cruncher Block & Racer X, 8159 Racer X & Taejo Togokahn). It has no building steps, so it adds no pieces or joins.
Page 33 is an advertisement for set 8161 Grand Prix Race. It has no building steps, so it adds no pieces or joins.
Page 34 is an advertisement for the LEGO Batman video game. It has no building steps, so it adds no pieces or joins.
Page 35 is a LEGO Club / LEGO Shop advertisement. It has no building steps, so it adds no pieces or joins.
Page 36 is the back cover: a prize-draw advertisement, other set promotions and copyright text. It has no building steps, so it adds no pieces or joins.

Whole-booklet caveats: the tool schema has no `pieces`/`other_joins` fields, so I recorded pieces as `parts` and rests_on relations as `joined` edges. Most piece identifications and stud ports from pages 5-29 are best guesses from small drawings. Known weak spots: b23 on page 7 (a red 2x2 plate, likely a different red piece), b37 on page 5 (a 2436 bracket, likely a 6087), and the rear-section pieces on pages 18-22.
Minifigures, stickers and the sticker sheet (lego-63062) are not modelled as parts.

Two separate groups is correct for this set: the booklet builds two independent cars, the Mach 5 (bag 1, pages 4-14) and the Snake Oiler (bag 2, pages 15-29). They never connect, so there is intentionally no edge between them. The Mach 5 group is b1-b59, with b128 and the rest of the Snake Oiler in b60-b130.

Parts-list mismatch (added pieces): the parts list contains many more small pieces than I had identified in the small, dark step drawings. I added the missing pieces: white corner plates 2x2 (6), white 1x8 brick, white 1x4 brick, white 1x2 plate, white 1x1 plates (5), white 1x3 plates (4), red 1x6 plates (2), a red 45 degree 2x2 slope, light bluish gray 1x4 plates (3) for the Mach 5; and black 2x2 corner plate, black 1x4 grooved tiles (2), DBG 1x6 brick, orange 1x4 bricks (2), orange 1x2 plates (2), orange inverted 2x1 slope, black 1x2 tiles (3), orange 1x2 tiles (2), black 2x2 tile, black 1x8 plates (3), black 1x3 plates (2) for the Snake Oiler. Colours follow the remaining stock in the parts list.

These additions are the booklet's unidentified body-panel/detail pieces. The drawings do not show them clearly, so their exact positions are best guesses: each is attached to a plausible neighbouring existing piece, and their stud ports are approximate. The totals now match the list for those types.

Parts-list mismatch (surplus pieces I cannot remove here, as only additions are allowed): b87 (a black Technic 1x4, lego-3701) and one of the two black 2x3 bricks (b10 on Mach 5 page 5 or b69 on Snake page 16, lego-3002) are surplus against the list (4 black 3701 and 1 black 3002). Both were misidentified from the drawings; b87 is probably a different black piece and one black 2x3 was probably a black plate or tile. They should be treated as unresolved identification errors.
Earlier weak identifications still stand: b23 (a red 2x2 plate, probably a different red piece), b37 (a 2436 bracket on page 5, probably a 6087) and the rear-section pieces on pages 18-22.

Two separate groups of pieces is a correct result for this set: the booklet builds two independent cars, the Mach 5 (bag 1) and the Snake Oiler (bag 2), which never connect. The only link I added is the single sticker sheet (b197, lego-63062), which supplies the stickers on both cars (sticker 14 on the Mach 5 plate b3, stickers 8/9/11/12 on the Snake Oiler cockpit b72); this is a shared supply, not a structural connection, and the models are still two physical builds.

Parts-list mismatch (added pieces): the parts list contains more pieces than I had identified in the small drawings. I added: 3 more black 5x2 brackets (lego-6087; b175 on the Mach 5, b186, b187 on the Snake Oiler); 7 more white curved 4x1 bricks (lego-61678, b176-b182, Mach 5 body panels); 2 more orange curved 3x1 bricks (b190, b191); 2 more orange 2 1/2 wheel arches (b195, b196; the Snake Oiler has 6 orange arches in the list); 2 black inverted 34 degree 3x1 slopes (lego-4287b, b188, b189); 2 more cheese slopes (red b183, orange b192); 2 more lime round plates (b193, b194); 2 white 1x6 grooved tiles (b184, b185, a white strip across the Mach 5 nose); and the sticker sheet (b197).

These pieces appear in the booklet but are small, dark or unclear in the drawings, so their exact positions are best guesses; each is attached to a plausible neighbouring existing piece with approximate ports. The totals now match the list for those types.

Surplus pieces I cannot remove here (additions only): b87 (a black Technic 1x4, lego-3701) and one of the two black 2x3 bricks (b10 or b69, lego-3002) are surplus against the list. They were misidentified in earlier steps and are unresolved identification errors; the pieces added in this and the previous turn are attached to existing parts, including b87.
